segments.line: But here's the problem.
Everybody now thinks the sky eye can lift stones.
Hemiunu asks you how many blocks it can carry in a day. The
honest answer is zero.
One block in this pyramid weighs about two and a half tonnes.
Your drone weighs less than one kilo. The stone
is almost three thousand times heavier than the thing that's supposed to lift it. And there are about
two point three million blocks.
To finish in twenty years, they have to set one every two or three minutes, ten hours a day, for twenty years.
Your drone is not going to help with that.
Problem two: heat. Your
batteries are made to work up to forty degrees.
Summer afternoons here are around thirty- five in the shade, and there is no shade in the sky. At
noon the controller flashes a warning. Battery temperature too high.
So you can only fly early in the morning and in the evening. And then there's
the sand. It gets into everything, including the motors.
After one bad gust, your drone sounds like a coffee grinder. You
clean it with a tiny brush and a lot of hope.
Problem three. Every time you charge a battery, it wears out a little. After a few hundred charges, it holds a lot less. A
year, maybe two, and your magic is just a plastic bug.
Every flight is one flight closer to the last one. And then there's
the language. Nobody here speaks a word of English, and you don't speak a word of ancient Egyptian. Nobody does anymore. Nobody
alive in your time knows exactly how it sounded, because they wrote it down without the vowels.
Nefer is teaching you. So far you know three words.
Water.
Bread. And
no. And
the people stepping off the golden boat don't know any of that. All they know is that
a stranger has a god's eye in a box, and the king doesn't.
